# Climate Adaptation Briefing: Heat, Flood, Wildfire, Insurance Retreat (as of 2026-09-28)

Confidence note: figures marked (P) come from primary or trade sources (regulator, company release, Artemis, Howden). Figures marked (S) come from secondary or SEO-style blogs and should be verified before anyone relies on them. My search budget ran out mid-session, so the "weird signals" section is thinner than I wanted.

## 1. Biggest shifts (last 12-18 months)

- **Reinsurance is softening fast while retail homeowners are still being squeezed.** Howden Re: property-cat risk-adjusted rates down up to 25% at June 1 2026, after -16% at April 1 and -14.7% at Jan 1 (P). https://www.howdenre.com/news-insights/1-june-2026-property-catastrophe-renewals. Reinsurance capital is at a record, about $790B (S per https://www.insurancebusinessmag.com/reinsurance/news/breaking-news/catastrophe-reinsurance-prices-post-historic-annual-fall-583643.aspx). Howden says returns are compressing and could fall below cost of capital by 2027. Nothing in the report says savings reach homeowners. That lag is where the money is.
- **Cat bonds hit records.** H1 2026 issuance was about $18B across 83 deals, with about $65.6B outstanding and 12 first-time sponsors. 81% of risk capital is indemnity-triggered (P). https://www.artemis.bm/news/catastrophe-bond-market-records-that-were-broken-in-h1-2026/
- **Florida's market flipped, California's did not.** Citizens (FL) fell from 936,182 policies at the start of 2025 to about 395,000 (P). https://www.floridarealtors.org/news-media/news-articles/2026/01/citizens-policies-plummet-2025 and https://www.wusf.org/politics-issues/2025-12-27/citizens-property-insurance-now-has-fewer-than-400-000-policies. The California FAIR Plan had 696,562 policies in June 2026, up 8% since Sept 2025. Exposure was $768B, up 250% since Sept 2022 (S). https://beinsure.com/news/california-insurers-pledge-new-policies/. FAIR's 2026 rate hike was about 29.1% (https://www.kqed.org/news/12094860/california-fair-plan-announces-29-1-rate-hike-for-homeowners-this-fall).
- **The regulatory rulebook is being rewritten.**
  - California's Sustainable Insurance Strategy allows forward-looking cat models and reinsurance cost in rates, in exchange for an 85% writing commitment in distressed ZIPs. Zurich, Mercury and CSAA are expanding, but the June 2026 CDI release gave no numbers (P). https://www.insurance.ca.gov/0400-news/0102-alerts/2026/California-s-Insurance-Market-Strengthen.cfm
  - Colorado HB25-1182 has applied since July 1 2026. Insurers using wildfire models must disclose the parcel's score, credit documented mitigation, and offer an appeal (S). https://coloradosun.com/2026/07/18/colorado-homeowners-insurance-discounts-mitigation-hail/
  - Fannie and Freddie (LL-2026-03, Mar 18 2026) now accept actual-cash-value roof coverage on single-family homes and condos (P). https://www.insurancejournal.com/news/national/2026/03/20/862768.htm
- **Cooling is turning into a legal duty for landlords.**
  - Maryland: 80F cap in buildings of 10+ units, effective June 1 2026.
  - LA County (unincorporated): 82F cap enforced from Jan 1 2027. Small landlords need one habitable room by 2027 and all rooms by 2032.
  - NYC Local Law 2026/023: 78F cap, tenant opt-in from Mar 2028, owner duty from 2030.
  - Washington: landlords generally cannot bar portable cooling devices from June 11 2026.
  - Source: https://www.readyourlease.ai/guides/air-conditioning-heating-laws (S) and https://www.rhawa.org/blog/new-state-law-portable-cooling-devices-for-renters
- **Federal heat rule slipped.** OSHA's supplemental proposal is targeted for Dec 2026 and the final rule for Oct 2027. OSHA averaged about 2,400 heat inspections a year in 2022-2025. California (82F indoor trigger), Washington and Oregon already have their own rules (S). https://www.osha.gov/heat-exposure/rulemaking
- **Summer 2026 was a shock.** Reported: hottest US July on record at 76.89F. A European heatwave with a provisional death toll of about 38,000. A UK cooling-supply stockout with 900%+ inquiry spikes (S). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_North_American_heat_wave and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_European_heatwaves. DOE let PJM force data centers onto backup diesel (S). https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2026/7/3/us-heatwave-raises-alarms-over-ai-data-centre-energy-demands

## 2. Acute, quantified pain points

- **NFIP expires Sept 30 2026, two days from today.** More than 30 short-term extensions since FY2017. An extension is expected inside FY27 appropriations (P). https://www.nar.realtor/flood-insurance/faq-national-flood-insurance-program-expires-september-30-2026. In the 2010 lapse, about 1,400 closings a day were delayed or cancelled (S). Risk Rating 2.0 premiums must roughly double toward full risk, with median $689 versus $1,288 needed (S). https://www.congress.gov/crs-product/IN11777
- **Aerial-imagery nonrenewals.** Homeowners report being dropped over roof photos, including a Florida owner with 52 claim-free years and no in-person inspection (S). https://www.aol.com/finance/no-protection-florida-homeowner-dropped-105500990.html. California AB 75 (notice, copy of photos, dispute and remediation window) became operative July 1 2026. CT, NH and PA regulators say imagery alone is insufficient, and a NY bill is pending (S). https://blog.pia.org/2026/05/06/n-y-bill-would-set-standards-for-use-of-aerial-imagery-in-homeowners-insurance/. Even so, "owners still have to prove their case."
- **Mitigation credit is unclaimable in practice.** The retrofit baseline is $8K-25K (S). Insurer discounts run 5-35% (S, https://roofvista.com/resources/guides/california-wildfire-prepared-designation-guide). The Colorado Sun quotes a homeowner on "1,000 bucks towards a $75,000 metal roof." Boulder's rebate is capped at $500. Premiums "quintupled in a decade" for one Parker, CO owner.
- **Florida condos.** SB 4D inspections plus milestone and reserve-study requirements mean carriers want documents before they bind a master policy. Reported special assessments are $50K-$200K+ per unit, and insurance can be 40-60% of the HOA budget (S). https://www.liveinsurancenews.com/florida-condo-owners-assessments/8576147/
- **Post-fire rebuild gap.** Only about 13% of affected Palisades single-family owners have begun rebuilding. Insurer estimates were about $462/sq ft against contractor budgets up to $1,065/sq ft (S). https://www.smobserved.com/story/2026/03/30/news/very-few-pacific-palisades-residents-pull-building-permits-or-plan-to-rebuild-heres-why/9748.html
- **Trades bottleneck.** HVAC labor shortages are structural, and installs and repairs are slower (S). https://hvac365.com/blog/hvac-labor-shortage-worsens-ahead-of-summer-peak/

## 3. Where the money is flowing

- **Climate-risk data is consolidating.** MSCI bought First Street for $120M cash plus a two-year earn-out, closing Q3 2026 (P). https://www.msci.com/discover-msci/media-room/msci-acquires-first-street-to-enhance-physical-climate-risk-capabilities-for-financial-decision-making. Moody's already owns Four Twenty Seven and RMS. A cash price this modest suggests scoring alone is not a big venture outcome.
- **Parametric and wildfire startups are small.**
  - Kettle: about $25M total raised.
  - Satellites on Fire: $2.7M, working with Aon on a parametric product (https://www.theinsurer.com/parametric-insurer/news/wildfire-detection-startup-raises-27-million-and-plans-parametric-and-us-2026-04-08/).
  - Descartes: about $200M+ raised (S).
  - Crowded: risk scoring, parametric MGAs, cat bonds and wildfire detection.
- **Public money is unstable.** FEMA cancelled BRIC in April 2025. A court ordered it restored and FEMA reinstated it Mar 18 2026 with $1B. Applications closed July 23 2026 (https://www.fema.gov/press-release/20260325/fema-announces-1-billion-federal-funding-help-states-mitigate-impact). California launched a Safe Homes Grant in Jan 2026 for low- and moderate-income owners and a revolving loan program under SB 894 (S). https://readyfireone.com/learn/articles/california-home-hardening-grants

## 4. Underserved gaps and structural blind spots

- **A neutral evidence layer.** Insurers cannot advocate for the policyholder, and homeowners cannot cheaply prove roof condition, vent type or 5-ft clearance. New laws (AB 75, HB25-1182) now require disputes and documented credits, but nobody owns the workflow.
- **Small landlords and HOA boards.** They face cooling duties and reserve-study or insurance underwriting packages, and lack tools. LA County's phase-in (one room by 2027) fits small operators.
- **Retail pass-through lag.** Reinsurance is softening, but primary carriers file slowly, and regulators are the choke point. Insurers cannot cut rates fast without hurting their own rate cases.
- **Cash buyers of "uninsurable" homes.** Financing fails, so these sell to cash buyers at a discount (S). https://www.fortune.com/2024/09/24/uninsurable-homes-selling-all-cash-discount
- **Neglected perils.** Hail drives 26-54% of Colorado premiums (S). Heat and smoke business-interruption cover for outdoor workforces is barely productized.

## 5. Weird signals

- Florida "take-out" insurers get Citizens' policy data to cherry-pick which policies to assume (https://mynews13.com/fl/orlando/news/2026/05/07/citizens-insurance-private-data-information). A CBS investigation (headline only, unverified detail) says whistleblowers allege owners of a receiving company diverted millions to investors (https://www.cbsnews.com/projects/2026/florida-insurance/). The fast Citizens shrinkage may have moved risk onto thinly capitalized carriers.
- Howden's own note that reinsurer returns may fall below cost of capital by 2027. A soft cycle and a growing protection gap can coexist, and the reversal would hit the retail layer first.
- Only 13% rebuilding in the Palisades, more than 18 months after the fire. Lot-sale liquidity, builder-financing and underinsurance-bridging may be a bigger market than rebuilding services.
- Cooling mandates arrive on a 2027-2032 phase-in for small landlords, so retrofit demand is pre-scheduled and predictable, unlike disasters.
- IBHS Wildfire Prepared Home just expanded to Washington (https://www.insurance.wa.gov/about-us/news/2026/ibhs-wildfire-prepared-home-designations-now-available-washington), which suggests home-hardening certification is going national.

# Food & Agriculture Briefing (as of 2026-09-28)

Coverage note: the 200-call web-search budget ran out mid-research, so the food-waste, farm-software and generic-semaglutide angles are thin. Figures marked (aggregator) come from low-authority sources and should be verified.

## 1. Biggest shifts, last 12-18 months

- **GLP-1s now move grocery baskets.**
  - Households cut grocery spend 5.3% within 6 months of starting a GLP-1 (more than 8% for higher-income households) and restaurant spend about 8% ([Cornell via Food Business News](https://www.foodbusinessnews.net/articles/29532-glp-1-users-cut-food-spending-by-53), [ScienceDaily](https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/01/260112001029.htm)).
  - Users buy fewer sweets (61%) and salty snacks (56%) and more fresh produce (44%) and packaged protein (35%) ([PwC](https://www.pwc.com/us/en/industries/consumer-markets/library/glp-1-consumer-trends.html), [FTI](https://www.fticonsulting.com/insights/articles/glp-1-drugs-rewriting-rules-food-beverage)).
  - The oral Wegovy pill launched in January 2026 at $149-299/month self-pay. It passed 5M total scripts across the GLP-1 launches by Q2 ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/01/05/first-glp-1-pill-for-obesity-from-novo-nordisk-launches-in-the-us.html)). Roughly 12% of Americans now use a GLP-1 ([Food Chain Magazine](https://foodchainmagazine.com/americas-protein-craze-is-driving-a-global-whey-shortage/)).
  - One estimate puts the annual US CPG sales hit at about $32B, with snacks and confectionery down 12.4% (aggregator: [mealfan](https://mealfan.com/glp-1-restaurant-cpg-impact-2026/)).
- **Protein is a supply crisis.**
  - 70% of Americans say they are trying to eat more protein, up from 59% four years ago.
  - Whey protein concentrate is up 108% in two years, isolate reaches $14/lb, and some suppliers are sold out through 2026. Cottage cheese consumption is up 15-20% ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/06/28/america-cant-get-enough-protein-the-dairy-industry-cant-keep-up.html), [GreenQueen](https://www.greenqueen.com.hk/whey-shortage-price-alternative-protein-fermentation-plant-based/)).
  - The binding constraint is downstream whey-processing capacity and cheese output, not raw milk ([UW Extension](https://farms.extension.wisc.edu/articles/high-protein-whey-and-cottage-cheese-a-structural-explainer/)).
- **Input shock from the Iran war and the Strait of Hormuz.**
  - About a third of seaborne fertilizer trade transits Hormuz. Urea spiked from about $400 to more than $850/t in April, then fell back to about $453 by June ([World Bank](https://blogs.worldbank.org/en/opendata/fertilizer-prices-surge-as-strait-of-hormuz-disruptions-tighten-), [WTO](https://www.wto.org/english/blogs_e/data_blog_e/blog_dta_10jul26_451_e.htm), [farmdoc](https://farmdocdaily.illinois.edu/2026/03/strait-of-hormuz-closure-and-fertilizer-supply-risks-for-us-agriculture.html)).
  - Farm-side figures: diesel up 80%, fertilizer up 15% year over year, farm bankruptcies up 19% in the 12 months to June. Major row crops are projected to lose money for a fourth straight year ([NPR](https://www.nprillinois.org/2026-09-25/american-farmers-are-hurting-and-worried-about-their-futures)).
  - Soybeans lose about $75 per harvested acre, exports run 15-20% behind normal, and a $12B aid package was approved in December 2025. Nearly half of 400 farmers surveyed by Purdue said they are worse off than a year ago ([PBS](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/nation/already-under-financial-pressure-farmers-squeezed-further-by-tariffs-and-iran-war)).
- **Beef.** Retail beef hit a record $9.64/lb in April (+13% year over year) with the smallest herd in 75 years. The Mexican feeder-cattle halt removes about 1.2M head a year, and New World screwworm has been confirmed in Texas cattle ([CNN](https://www.cnn.com/2026/06/09/business/what-consumers-should-know-about-screwworm), [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-06-10/beef-prices-hit-record-in-may-as-screwworm-impact-still-looms), [Dallas Fed](https://www.dallasfed.org/research/swe/2026/swe2612)).
- **Regulatory clocks.**
  - FDA aims to phase out petroleum-based dyes by December 2027. Walmart private label goes dye-free in January 2027.
  - Products containing FD&C dyes are about 4% of items but $57.8B in sales. Demand for natural colorants is projected to rise 400-500%, and the US is 98% import-dependent for annatto. Reformulation costs $50k-500k per SKU and takes 12-24+ months to validate ([Bakery&Snacks](https://www.bakeryandsnacks.com/Article/2026/09/01/us-food-dye-phase-out-puts-natural-color-supply-chain-under-pressure/)).
  - 22 states have SNAP soda/candy restrictions in effect or pending, though a June 2026 federal ruling (Aragon v. Rollins) blocked waivers in five of them ([The Hill](https://thehill.com/homenews/nexstar_media_wire/5796610-4-more-states-will-add-restrictions-on-snap-purchases-in-april/)).
  - FDA and USDA sent a first federal ultra-processed food definition for final review, alongside GRAS reform ([AJMC](https://www.ajmc.com/view/fda-proposes-gras-rule-advances-ultra-processed-food-definition)).
  - The EU has binding food-waste cuts pending: 30% per capita in retail, food service and households, and 10% in processing, by 2030 ([IGD](https://www.igd.com/articles/2026-european-grocery-retail-legislation-outlook/72733)).
- **Farm labor.**
  - The workforce reportedly shrank by at least 155,000 after the immigration crackdown. Strawberry and almond growers lost up to 30% of harvest crews in Jan-Mar 2026 ([VisaVerge](https://www.visaverge.com/news/trumps-immigration-policies-and-their-impact-on-u-s-agriculture/), a secondary source).
  - About 40% of hired crop labor is undocumented. H-2A visas exceeded 300k in 2024.
  - The October 2025 wage-rule change cuts H-2A pay. EPI estimates $4.4-5.4B a year in farmworker wage losses and growth toward 500k H-2A jobs ([EPI](https://www.epi.org/blog/trumps-new-h-2a-wage-rule-will-radically-cut-the-wages-of-all-farmworkers-new-estimates-show-farmworkers-stand-to-lose-4-4-to-5-4-billion-annually-under-dols-updated-adverse-effec/)).

## 2. Quantified pain points

- **Input squeeze with no pricing power.** "Our biggest struggles are our inputs... so much drastic markup" ([PBS](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/nation/already-under-financial-pressure-farmers-squeezed-further-by-tariffs-and-iran-war)).
- **Repair and downtime.** Repair restrictions cost US farmers about $4.2B a year (about $3.3k per farm) ([Moneywise/PIRG](https://moneywise.com/news/top-stories/john-deere-has-agreed-to-pay-99-million-to-farmers-over-claims-theyre-monopolizing-repairs-and-overcharging-farmers)). Deere's $99M settlement obliges it to open diagnostic and repair tools for 10 years.
- **Unharvested crops.** Grapes, blueberries and peaches rotted in the field in 2025 for lack of labor. Late or absent H-2A arrivals mean lost revenue and waste.
- **Protein buyers can't source whey.** Buyers are shifting from sustainability goals to supply-chain risk mitigation ([GreenQueen](https://www.greenqueen.com.hk/whey-shortage-price-alternative-protein-fermentation-plant-based/)).
- **CPG and food service.** Manufacturers face dye reformulation deadlines and volume loss. 48% of GLP-1 users say they would dine out more if smaller portions were offered ([Restaurant Business](https://www.restaurantbusinessonline.com/consumer-trends/not-all-glp-1-users-are-dining-out-or-spending-less-find-new-surveys)).
- **Spray drones.** DJI was added to the FCC Covered List in December 2025. DJI Agras hardware runs about 80% of the US spray-drone market, and the new T55 and T100 have no committed US launch ([DroneXL](https://dronexl.co/2026/07/01/dji-agras-t55-and-t100-launch-globally-fcc-drone-ban/)). The Texas Farm Bureau warns of limited drones and parts.

## 3. Where money is flowing

- **Overall (2025).**
  - Agrifoodtech funding was $16.2B (-3%) across 12% fewer deals. Upstream drew $9B (+7%).
  - Debt was 18.2% of the total, the highest in a decade. Agrifood climate tech rose to $3.9B from $2.8B. Wonder raised $600M.
  - Deeptech at seed gets a 78% premium that vanishes by Series B ([AgFunder News](https://agfundernews.com/agrifoodtech-funding-is-flat-the-interesting-part-is-where-it-isnt)).
- **Alt protein.**
  - Funding fell to $881M in 2025 from $1.1B. Plant-based rose 39% to $450M, fermentation fell 43% to $357M, and cultivated fell 48% to $74M.
  - H1 2026 raised only $197M, of which $132M was fermentation. More than 70 alt-protein companies have merged, been acquired or shut down since September 2024 ([FoodNavigator](https://www.foodnavigator.com/Article/2026/02/18/alternative-protein-funding-shifts-in-2026/), [vegconomist](https://vegconomist.com/studies-numbers/gfis-2026-state-of-industry-reports-detail-mixed-year-alternative-proteins-across-three-sectors/)).
  - Beyond Meat carries roughly $1.2B in debt and faces Nasdaq delisting risk ([Food Institute](https://foodinstitute.com/focus/beyond-meat-on-the-verge-of-financial-ruin/)).
  - Verley raised a €32M Series A for precision-fermented whey. It is FDA-cleared and claims price competitiveness with conventional whey ([GreenQueen](https://www.greenqueen.com.hk/verley-precision-fermentation-funding-animal-free-whey-protein/)).
- **Robotics and autonomy.**
  - Weeding and field robotics took about $180M, roughly 27% of tracked precision-ag capital in 2025. Ecorobotix raised a $105M Series D ([Precision Farming Dealer](https://www.precisionfarmingdealer.com/articles/7113-autonomous-weeding-robots-lead-2025-precision-ag-funding)).
  - Sabanto's Series B in July 2026 was led by Leaps by Bayer with Yara participating ([Fertilizer Daily](https://www.fertilizerdaily.com/20260717-sabanto-series-b/)).
  - Deere's autonomy kit costs about $40-45k plus $10k a year ([AgWeb](https://www.agweb.com/news/john-deere-introducing-next-generation-perception-autonomy-kits)).
  - Oishii acquired Tortuga AgTech ([The Packer](https://www.thepacker.com/news/packer-tech/oishii-acquires-robotics-company-tortuga-agtech-extends-harvesting-capabilities)).
- **Food waste.** Small European rounds: Foodforecast €8M, Freshflow €6.5M ([EU-Startups](https://www.eu-startups.com/2026/02/german-ai-foodtech-startup-foodforecast-raises-e8-million-to-tackle-ultra-fresh-food-wastage/)).
- **Crowded or damaged categories.** Plant-based meat (US sales declining), cultivated meat, vertical farming, and generic food-waste marketplaces and forecasting.
  - Vertical farming had 14 bankruptcies in 2025, including Plenty (about $1.19B raised) (aggregator: [Foodlore](https://foodlore.blog/why-vertical-farms-go-bankrupt/)).
  - Autonomous weeding is filling up fast.

## 4. Underserved gaps and structural blind spots

- **Post-GLP-1 formats.** Small-portion, high-protein, high-fiber, nutrient-dense products and menus. Incumbent P&Ls are built on volume and price-per-ounce, so shrinking portions cannibalizes revenue (inference).
- **Protein diversification.** Whey and casein are capped by cheese output. Buyers want non-dairy or fermentation sources, and Leaft (rubisco) and Alpine Bio (fractionated soy) are early entrants. The gap is functionality: whey uniquely gives clear drinks at pH 2.8-3.5 ([FoodNavigator](https://www.foodnavigator.com/Article/2026/07/24/in-a-global-shortage-what-are-the-alternatives-to-whey/)).
- **Natural color supply chain.** The US is almost fully import-dependent for annatto, butterfly pea and saffron, and demand is set to multiply. Domestic sourcing, extraction and stabilization is open, as is a reformulation-as-a-service business.
- **Mid-size and specialty farms.** They sit below the point where Deere's kits pay off. Orchard and vineyard retrofits (Bluewhite: 50k autonomous hours over 150k acres) show the model works.
- **Post-settlement repair diagnostics.** Deere must open its tools for a decade, which creates an independent repair software market.
- **Farmland succession.** One-third of landlords are 75 or older, and only about 1 in 4 farmers has a formal succession plan. Over 60% of farmland may change hands in 10-15 years ([Schrader](https://www.schraderauction.com/resources/farmland-succession-wave-landlords-over-75-estate-planning), [The Bullet](https://www.wwbl.com/2026/07/14/the-invisible-farmland-transfer-why-millions-of-acres-wont-hit-the-market/)).
- **Labor-arbitrage robots-as-a-service.** Per-box pricing near human wages removes capex risk for growers ([AgTecher](https://agtecher.com/en/robotics/tortuga/)). Robots reportedly pick at 50-60% of human speed but run about 20 hours a day.

## 5. Weird signals

- **Cocoa whiplash.** Cocoa went from more than $12,000/t in 2024 to about $3,845/t on May 20, 2026. Chocolate makers are reportedly restoring cocoa in recipes, which strands cocoa-alternative capacity such as Planet A Foods and Fermtech ([Prism News](https://www.prismnews.com/news/chocolate-makers-restore-cocoa-recipes-as-prices-plunge), [Bakery&Snacks](https://www.bakeryandsnacks.com/Article/2026/03/10/the-race-to-reinvent-cocoa-lab-grown-chocolate-and-cocoa-alternatives/)). Commodity-hedged alt-ingredient models are fragile.
- **The byproduct ate the product.** Whey, formerly a cheese waste stream, is now scarcer than the cheese, and factories are re-tooling for cottage cheese ([ZeroHedge](https://www.zerohedge.com/food/byproduct-ate-product-inside-americas-proteinmaxxing-cheese-glut)).
- **GLP-1 hits spirits and pets.**
  - US spirits sales fell 15.4% and Diageo's US tequila fell 23% ([Poached](https://blog.poachedjobs.com/2026/05/13/restaurant-business/restaurant-insights-news/is-glp-1-use-cutting-into-your-alcohol-sales/)).
  - "Ozempic for cats" is emerging, and pet spend is shifting from premiumization to medicalization ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/18/cats-glp-1-ozempic-pets-weight-loss.html)).
- **Vertical farming survivor.** AeroFarms is reportedly profitable after abandoning multi-site expansion and pivoting to microgreens ([Fast Company](https://www.fastcompany.com/91330232/aeorfarms-turned-itself-around-after-bankruptcy-is-it-a-sign-that-vertical-farming-can-succeed)). Niche and margin beat scale.
- **China's ag-biotech surge.** Agrifoodtech funding in China grew 43% and in South Korea 171% on state-backed biotech money, while US deeptech tops out below $200M rounds ([AgFunder News](https://agfundernews.com/agrifoodtech-funding-is-flat-the-interesting-part-is-where-it-isnt)).
- **Farmland "invisible transfer."** Millions of acres will move through estates rather than the open market, so listing-based land data will miss much of it.

# Briefing: Legal services, compliance and new regulation (as of 2026-09-28)

**Research limits, read first.** The session's WebSearch budget (200/200) was exhausted before this scout started, so I ran zero searches. I did not route around that by pointing WebFetch at search engines. Everything below comes from about 25 direct page fetches (Wikipedia, TechCrunch, LawSites, trackers). The fetch tool summarizes pages with a small model, and several sources were 404, 403 or blocked, including Reddit, ECHA, the EPA TSCA page and the EU Commission omnibus page. Items marked **[UNVERIFIED]** are secondary-source or from my own background knowledge. Nothing here is a primary-source legal reading.

## 1. Biggest shifts, last 12-18 months

The Act as originally passed said Aug 2026 and Aug 2027 (my background knowledge), so this looks like the Digital Omnibus delay. The page never names the Omnibus, so **[UNVERIFIED]** whether it is final.
  - GPAI (general-purpose AI) obligations have applied since Aug 2025, and the AI Office began Chapter V enforcement in Aug 2026 ([artificialintelligenceact.eu](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/)).
  - Fines run up to EUR 35M or 7% of turnover for prohibited practices, and EUR 15M or 3% for other operator duties ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_Intelligence_Act)).

  - EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) **reporting obligations began 11 Sep 2026**: 24-hour incident reporting to ENISA for anything with digital elements. Full application is 11 Dec 2027, and fines reach EUR 15M or 2.5% of turnover ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyber_Resilience_Act)).
  - EU Data Act: general applicability since 12 Sep 2025. Connected products must give users direct data access **by design from 12 Sep 2026** ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Data_Act_(European_Union))).

  - CBAM (carbon border levy) entered its definitive phase in 2026, and the UK CBAM starts 1 Jan 2027 across 8 sectors ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carbon_Border_Adjustment_Mechanism)).

  - The EU Directive 2024/1799 transposition deadline was **31 Jul 2026**. An EU repair platform is due by 1 Jan 2028 ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Right_to_repair)).

Deal size was not disclosed.

Legal-tech funding was $3.56B in H1 2025, up 44% year on year ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legal_technology)).
- **The frontier labs are entering.** OpenAI released "Astra for Law" on 17 Sep 2026. It bundles a legal search index over 230M+ URLs, sourced from the Free Law Project's CourtListener, and scored 54% vs 38.7% on legal research benchmarks. It ships via API to Harvey and Legora and through a "Trusted Access" program for Am Law 200 firms, with 26 vendor plugins including Thomson Reuters and iManage ([LawSites](https://www.lawnext.com/2026/09/openai-releases-astra-for-law-a-gpt-6-model-configured-for-legal-work.html)).

# Space Economy Briefing: cheap launch, satellite data, direct-to-cell, earth observation
Date: 2026-09-28

**Provenance and confidence.** The WebSearch budget (200/200) was exhausted before this scout ran, so zero searches were done. Everything tagged [F] comes from direct page fetches (news homepages, Wikipedia pages, company pages), which a small model summarized, so treat figures as reported and not audited. Forums and Reddit were not reachable, so section 2 is mostly inference. Items tagged [P] are prior knowledge (cutoff June 2026) and are unverified. Some fetched summaries were stale or garbled, and I say where.

## 1. Biggest shifts, last 12-18 months
- **Starship reached orbit on 2026-09-28.** [F] Payload Space and TechCrunch both report it, and Satellite Today says it cut a 10-hour mission short after an engine issue. Payload calls it the 14th test flight and TechCrunch calls it the first orbital attempt, so the count is inconsistent. Orbital-class Starship implies a step-change in $/kg and in Starlink V3 deployment. Sources: https://payloadspace.com, https://techcrunch.com/category/space/, https://www.satellitetoday.com
- **Launch supply is exploding and the competitors are now funded.** [F] Stoke Space raised a $1B Series E in Sept 2026 after extending its Series D to $860M in Feb 2026, and unveiled Nova Block 2 at 15 t to LEO (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stoke_Space). The Exploration Company raised $450M (Sept 2026), Impulse Space's Series D extension took the round to $808M, and Deep Blue Aerospace is raising about $300M (https://spacenews.com). 2025 had 321 orbital launches and 4,517 satellites deployed, versus 223 launches in 2023 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_industry).
- **Reliability is still fragile outside SpaceX.** [F] AST SpaceMobile's BlueBird 7 was lost on New Glenn on 2026-04-19 when it failed to reach operational orbit. BlueBird 6 flew on India's LVM3 in Dec 2025 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AST_SpaceMobile). Non-SpaceX launch remains a bottleneck for anyone building constellations.
- **Starlink is now a giant with falling ARPU.** [F] Subscribers went from 8.9M (Dec 2025) to 10.3M (Mar 2026) to 12M (Jun 2026), about +35% in six months. ARPU fell from $81 to $66 over one quarter (-19%). There are about 10,413 satellites in orbit, and 2025 revenue was $11.4B with $4.4B operating income (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starlink). The mix is shifting to cheaper and international plans.
- **The spectrum land-grab settled.** [F] EchoStar sold spectrum to AT&T for $23B (announced 2025-08-26, closed 2026-07-28) and to SpaceX for $17B in cash and stock (announced 2025-09-08) (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EchoStar). SpaceX now holds its own mobile spectrum, so it is a direct-to-cell operator and not just a carrier partner. Carriers are signing satellite-mobile partnerships in bulk (Satellite Today, Sept 15-16: "Key Questions Remain Unresolved", "European MNOs Disagree on the Value of Satellite D2D"). Beeline Kazakhstan launched Starlink Mobile service on 2026-09-28.
- **Consolidation.** [F] Rocket Lab agreed on 2026-06-29 to buy Iridium for about $8B ($27 cash plus stock, notional $54 per share, close expected mid-2027). Iridium shareholders have approved it, and Rocket Lab's CFO said more M&A is coming. Iridium had 2.627M billable subscribers at 2026-06-30 and $871.7M of 2025 revenue (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iridium_Communications, https://payloadspace.com).
- **Defense is the demand floor.** [F] Golden Dome has about $37-38B of FY25-26 funding, a cost estimate raised to $185B (Mar 2026), more than 1,000 qualifying offerors, and a reported $2B SpaceX 600-satellite award (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Dome_(missile_defense_system)). Northrop is delivering 21 data-relay satellites, and the US military confirmed deploying weapons to orbit (Sept 15, 2026).

## 2. Acute pain points (mostly inferred)
- [F, indirect] Satellite-mobile partnerships are multiplying, but "key questions remain unresolved" (Satellite Today, Sept 15). European MNOs disagree on whether D2D is worth paying for. Carriers do not know how to price it or how to differentiate it from the SpaceX and T-Mobile offering. That is a wedge for neutral tooling, such as coverage assurance, QoS measurement, billing and roaming brokers.
- [F, indirect] Launch and satellite-bus providers are raising nine-figure rounds (EnduroSat $205M, Aerospacelab supplying Lockheed, Hubble $200M), which suggests bus and payload integration is capacity-constrained.
- [P, unverified] EO customers complain about tasking latency, cloud and revisit gaps, and the cost of turning pixels into decisions. Analytics is still seen as the unsolved layer. This needs verification.
- [P, unverified] Operators face rising conjunction-screening load and rising insurance costs as LEO passes 10k Starlinks. This also needs verification.

## 3. Where the money is flowing, and what is crowded
- [F] Launch and mobility are the hot categories, with Stoke $1B, Exploration Co. $450M, Impulse $808M round total, and Deep Blue about $300M.
- [F] Space IoT and Bluetooth-to-satellite is hot. Hubble Network raised a $200M Series C at a $1.6B valuation (Sept 28, 2026), bringing its total funding to $300M. Its Series B was $70M in Sept 2025 (https://payloadspace.com). It says it has 6 operational satellites and next-generation satellites in 2027, and it claims 100M+ terrestrial access points, coverage in about 2,500 cities, and detection at 4 dBm in the future versus +20 dBm today (https://hubble.com).
- [F] Space Capital reports $488B invested in the space economy since 2009 across 3,000+ companies (https://www.spacecapital.com/quarterly). European rounds are hot: Payload counts the EnduroSat raise as the third nine-figure European space raise in two weeks.
- [F] EO is mature and government-anchored. Planet has a EUR240M Germany contract (July 2025), a $230M SKY Perfect JSAT deal for 10 Pelican satellites (Jan 2025), and a Berlin factory (Sept 2025) that doubles Pelican production. It targets up to 10 revisits per day (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Planet_Labs).
- **Crowded:** launch vehicles, satellite buses, broadband constellations (Meridian Space is planning another), and generic EO imagery.

## 4. Underserved segments and structural gaps (analysis, partly inference)
- **Anything that requires neutrality from SpaceX.** Starlink is both the network and a competitor to carriers, so carriers, governments and enterprises want a hedge. That means multi-constellation and multi-orbit aggregation, sovereign backup, and independent QoS auditing.
- **Post-Starship in-space services.** Cheaper mass to orbit raises demand for power, compute, manufacturing and servicing. Signals are Star Catcher (power-beaming demo ready to launch), Outpost (in-space manufacturing service launched, first mission no earlier than 2028), Besxar (orbital chip fab) and AstroForge (AI commanding of DeepSpace-2). Almost all of it is pre-revenue.
- **Decision products on top of commodity pixels.** Incumbents sell imagery or subscriptions, and the buyer wants an answer such as insurance, credit, compliance, or methane and CO2 attribution (Planet's Tanager hyperspectral satellite launched Aug 2024). Vertical analytics tied to a regulated buyer remains open.
- **The gap between "phone texts from space" and "phone has a data plan from space".** Iridium NTN Direct is expected later in 2026 (live demos as of July 2026), and AST is spectrum-rich (45 MHz L-band approval from the FCC on 2025-06-13) but launch-constrained. There is room for terminal, chipset, enterprise and vertical products that use whichever network wins.

# Briefing: Gaming, entertainment, live experiences, fandoms (as of 2026-09-28)

**Method caveat.** The session's WebSearch budget (200/200) was already spent, so I ran zero searches. This brief comes from about 35 WebFetch pulls, almost all Wikipedia snapshots current to Sept 2026. Newzoo and GamesIndustry.biz were blocked, and Pollstar is paywalled. I had no Reddit or forum access, so the pain points below come from documented events (lawsuits, regulator orders, breaches), not practitioner quotes. Figures are as those pages report them and are not independently verified. Anything marked *(inference)* is my reading, not a sourced fact.

## 1. Biggest shifts (last 12-18 months)
- **Hardware now gets more expensive over its life, because AI data centers are eating the RAM supply.** Valve's Steam Machine launched 2026-06-29 at $1,049 (512GB) and $1,349 (2TB), against an early target of about $800 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steam_Machine). Xbox Series prices rose on tariffs and RAM shortages, and the next Xbox ("Project Helix") is likely late 2027 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_(brand)). Switch 2 launched at $449.99 (June 2025) and goes to $499.99 on 2026-09-01. Some games are $80, and 23.68M units had sold by 2026-06-30 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nintendo_Switch_2).
- **Leveraged buyouts and mega-mergers are reshaping ownership.**
  - EA's $55B LBO closed 2026-08-04. PIF holds 93.4%, $20B is JPMorgan debt, and the owners plan to "reduce operating costs by incorporating AI throughout" (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts).
  - Paramount Skydance's $110B all-cash deal for WBD won DOJ approval on 2026-06-12, and California settled on 2026-09-21 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Bros._Discovery).
  - Ubisoft took €1.16B from Tencent for 25% of Vantage Studios (a €4B valuation). Headcount fell from 18,666 (Sep 2024) to 16,590 (Mar 2026), FY26 net loss was €1.516B, and six games were cancelled in Jan 2026 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ubisoft).
- **GTA VI launches 2026-11-19 at $79.99.** Preorders opened 2026-06-25, day-one estimates run $1.2B+, and other publishers are rescheduling around it (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Theft_Auto_VI).
- **Age assurance is becoming mandatory plumbing for gaming and social platforms.**
  - Roblox required global age checks in Jan 2026, added age tiers ("Kids" under 9, "Select" 9-15) in June 2026, and was designated an EU Very Large Online Platform in Aug 2026 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roblox).
  - Discord announced mandatory face-scan or ID checks worldwide in Mar 2026, with rollout targeted for late Sept 2026 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discord).
  - The UK Online Safety Act set a 2025-07-25 enforcement deadline. VPN downloads surged (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Online_Safety_Act_2023).
- **Ticketing hit a regulatory reckoning.**
  - The FTC's all-in pricing rule took effect 2025-05-12. The FTC and 7 states sued Live Nation in Sept 2025 over resale, alleging $3.7B in resale fees from 2019 to 2024 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ticketmaster).
  - A federal jury found Live Nation liable for illegal monopolization on 2026-04-15. The Live Nation page also lists a DOJ settlement on 2026-03-09, and I could not reconcile the two, so the remedies are unclear (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment).
  - Live Nation's 2025 revenue was $25.2B.
- **App-store fee walls are cracking.** Epic won an April 2025 ruling that Apple cannot charge fees on third-party storefronts. The Epic Store returned to US iOS in May 2025, and Epic charges 0% on a game's first $1M, then 12% (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epic_Games_Store).

## 2. Acute, quantified pain points
- **Games disappear when servers die, and buyers have no recourse.**
  - The Stop Killing Games EU petition got about 1.448M signatures, of which 1,294,188 were verified valid. The EU Commission declined a mandatory playability rule on 2026-06-16 and proposed a voluntary industry code of conduct by end of 2026.
  - *Anthem* shut down 2026-01-12. Of 738 tracked games, 68% are unplayable or at risk.
  - French group UFC-Que Choisir sued Ubisoft over *The Crew* (2026-03-31), and a suit was filed against Sony over PS5 physical-disc cessation (Aug 2026) (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stop_Killing_Games).
- **Identity data collected for compliance is itself a liability.**
  - Discord's Sept 2025 breach was claimed to have exposed 2.1M government ID photos, and 70,000 users were affected (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discord).
  - Photo age checks were beaten using *Death Stranding* character images (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Online_Safety_Act_2023).
  - Small studios and communities face the same mandates with none of the compliance budget *(inference)*.
- **Fans distrust ticket pricing and resale.** Oasis tickets rose from £135 to £350+ under dynamic pricing, and the UK CMA opened an investigation on 2024-09-05. In June 2026 the CMA ordered StubHub to refund 50,000+ customers for drip pricing. StubHub's World Cup 2026 tickets failed to reach buyers, and class actions were filed in New York and British Columbia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/StubHub).
- **Generative AI use triggers backlash and needs provenance.** *Clair Obscur* lost two Indie Game Awards over AI textures (removed before shipping). Eurogamer scored *ARC Raiders* 2/5 partly over AI voices. NVIDIA's DLSS 5 was called "AI slop." Valve requires AI disclosure on Steam (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence_in_video_games). No standard exists for proving what is AI-made *(inference)*.
- **Release-date collisions hurt indies.** *Silksong* had about 5.2M wishlists, sold 7M+ copies by Dec 2025, and pushed several indie titles to delay after its date was announced (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollow_Knight:_Silksong).
- **Counterfeits hit collectibles.** The US CPSC warned about fake "Lafufu" Labubu dolls on 2025-08-18 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_Mart).

## 3. Where money is flowing (and what is crowded)
- **Sovereign money:** PIF's $55B EA deal. It also funds the Esports World Cup Foundation, with prize pools of $71.5M (2025) and $75M (2026, moved to Paris) and a $20M club partner program across 40 orgs (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Esports_World_Cup). The Saudi-Olympic Esports Games partnership was terminated 2025-10-30 and the Games moved to 2027 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Esports).
- **Prediction markets:** Kalshi went from about $11B (Dec 2025) to $22B (May 2026, TCV-led). 89% of its 2025 revenue was sports, $871M was wagered on Super Bowl Sunday 2026, and it added 3M users for the World Cup. States are fighting it, and Nevada reached a permanent shutdown agreement (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalshi).
- **Live venues and IP-in-space:**
  - Live Nation is buying arenas in Paris and Copenhagen and put Ticketmaster inside Spotify in June 2026.
  - Sphere grossed $420.5M from 1.3M tickets in 2024 and is planning venues in Maryland, Tokyo and Abu Dhabi (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sphere_(venue)).
  - Meow Wolf has Los Angeles (late 2026) and New York in the pipeline (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meow_Wolf).
- **Microdramas:** roughly $11B globally in 2025. ReelShort had about $700M revenue and 45M MAU, and DramaBox had $323M in 2024 revenue. US spend is about $1.3B a year, mostly women aged 30-60, with production at $50k-$250k for 50-70 episodes (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microdrama).
- **Collectibles:** Kickstarter's Cyberpunk trading card game raised $28.35M in April 2026 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kickstarter). Pokémon has sold 85B+ cards (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trading_card_game).
- **Crowded:** AAA publishing, ticket resale marketplaces, sports prediction markets, and Roblox-style UGC platforms *(inference)*. Big money is chasing the same few mass-market pools.

## 4. Underserved segments and structural gaps
- **Incumbents structurally cannot do these:**
  - Live Nation cannot credibly run fan-first, anti-resale primary ticketing while it is in litigation and its resale-fee revenue is under attack *(inference)*.
  - Publishers cannot promise server-life guarantees without admitting liability, as the Ubisoft suits show *(inference)*.

Overseas viewers were about 30% of viewership and roughly ¥10B of revenue (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hololive_Production).

- **Nomad compliance, not discovery.** Nomads.com sells lifetime membership for $1 (47,310 members), so information is commoditized; its "residence calendar for tax planning" hints at where value sits ([Nomads.com](https://nomads.com/)). The EES now tracks 90/180-day stays automatically, yet travelers can't easily see their own balance (inference).
- **Allocation, not fees.** Venice's day-tripper fee reportedly didn't reduce numbers ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tourism_in_Italy)); Mount Fuji uses a hard 4,000/day cap plus a JPY2,000 fee; Boracay caps ~19,200. Destinations need timed-entry and dispersal tooling, and levy administration is fragmented (Glasgow, Chicago, Balearics).

## 5. Weird signals

- **Booking lead times shrinking** (37.5 to 33 days) while demand "fragmented": last-minute, rerouted, value-driven travel, so rebooking and disruption products matter more.
- **Chinese outbound is changing shape.** Thailand lost a third of Chinese arrivals; Golden Week travelers "go farther and spend less on hotels" ([Skift](https://www.skift.com/)).
- **Anti-flight sentiment from inside the industry:** Intrepid's co-founder wants travelers "closer to home" ([Skift](https://www.skift.com/)).
- **Uber is reportedly "coming for STR"** while Airbnb adds mainstream tours, services, and (per Chesky) a softer stance on hotels/cars/flights ([Skift](https://www.skift.com/)).
- **Rogue-agent risk (single opinion source, unverified):** a HospitalityNet piece claims 2026 incidents of AI agents breaching systems and warns hotel concierge/booking agents often hold API access built for trusted staff; it recommends server-side authorization and human approval for irreversible actions ([HospitalityNet](https://hospitalitynet.org/opinion/4134583.html)). An "agent auth and audit layer for hospitality" is a possible angle if the risk proves real.

ideas.title: Bonded Escorts for Sedated Outpatient Patients
ideas.one_liner: A background-checked adult who legally receives your discharge instructions and takes you home after a colonoscopy or other sedated procedure, sold to the clinics that lose the slot when you have no ride.
ideas.customer: Independent GI groups and ambulatory surgery centers pay $65-95 per escorted visit. Solo agers and estranged or far-from-family adults pay $99-149 directly as a fallback.
ideas.problem: Most sedation centers will not proceed unless a responsible adult picks the patient up and hears the discharge instructions, and many refuse to release a sedated patient to a rideshare driver. Patients with no spouse, no nearby family, or no friend willing to sit through the aftermath of a bowel prep cancel, delay screening, or no-show. The clinic eats an empty high-margin slot. The patient feels embarrassed to ask and avoids the procedure.
ideas.solution: A regional network of vetted, insured escorts drawn from CNAs, retired nurses, EMTs and nursing students. The clinic scheduler adds one line to the booking call: 'No escort? Tap here and we will send one.' The escort meets the patient at the door, is named on the chart as the responsible adult, receives instructions, rides home with the patient, stays 20-30 minutes until the patient is settled, and texts a family contact. A clinic dashboard shows escort confirmed, so day-of cancellations for this reason disappear. Later add the required 24-hour post-anesthesia overnight companion, then cataract, oral surgery, and cosmetic and orthopedic day surgery.
ideas.why_now: The USPSTF lowered the colorectal screening start age to 45, which added millions of eligible patients. Procedures keep migrating to ambulatory surgery centers, which run on tight slot economics. The share of older adults living alone (solo agers) is at a record high. Checkr-style vetting and Stripe Connect-style payouts let a tiny team stand up a bonded, insured gig network in weeks. No incumbent sells 'the adult on the chart' to schedulers.
ideas.revenue_model: Per-visit fee paid by the clinic ($65-95, escort keeps about 60%) or patient-pay ($99-149). Add-ons include overnight post-anesthesia sitters billed hourly. Later, Medicare Advantage plans buy escort-with-transport as a supplemental benefit.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The escort rule is a liability policy, not a medical one, so what the clinic needs is a credentialed name on the chart that satisfies the discharge nurse, not a ride. Nobody sells to the scheduling desk, where the cancellation leak is measured in dollars per slot. The patient's real barrier is shame at asking a friend to witness a colonoscopy, which a professional stranger removes.
ideas.first_30_days: Pick one metro. Recruit 15 escorts from nursing-school boards and retired-nurse groups. Get a general and professional liability quote and run Checkr checks. Visit 10 GI practices and offer a free 30-day pilot where they pay only when an escort saves a slot that would have cancelled. Launch a landing page and a Twilio text line, and buy Google Ads on searches like 'colonoscopy no one to drive me home'. Run dispatch from a spreadsheet. Goal: 40 escorted procedures and 3 signed clinics.

ideas.title: Medicaid Work-Rule Retention for Hospitals and Plans
ideas.one_liner: A text-first service that proves work hours and exemptions on behalf of Medicaid members, paid per retained member by the hospitals and health plans that would otherwise lose them.
ideas.customer: Safety-net hospitals, FQHC networks and Medicaid managed-care plans in expansion states. They pay roughly $4-12 per retained member per month or a fee per successful report.
ideas.problem: Under the 2025 budget law (OBBBA), expansion adults aged 19-64 must document about 80 hours a month of work, school or volunteering, or prove an exemption, with more frequent renewals. Deadlines start no later than January 1, 2027, with limited state extensions. Arkansas in 2018 showed that people mostly lost coverage from reporting failures, not from ineligibility. Members lose coverage over paperwork. Hospitals and plans then lose revenue and absorb uncompensated care.
ideas.solution: A retention layer that sits on the member side. It works over SMS and WhatsApp in multiple languages. It connects to the member's payroll, gig-platform earnings, school enrollment or caregiver records to auto-assemble monthly proof. It screens for the many exemptions (medically frail, parents of young children, substance-use treatment, recent release) and generates provider attestation letters from the clinic's own visit. It submits in each state's format, using portal automation and mail-in where needed. It nags before deadlines. A dashboard shows the plan or hospital which members are at risk before the coverage cliff. The same engine later covers SNAP work rules.
ideas.why_now: The law was signed in July 2025, and federal guidance and state build-outs are happening now for the 2027 start. Some states, such as Georgia with Pathways, already run work-reporting programs. The large incumbents (state-agency contractors) build for the state side, not for retention on the member side. Hospital CFOs are modeling large expansion-population losses this budget cycle. LLM agents plus computer-use can drive dozens of clunky state portals that never had APIs. Gig and payroll data connections make proof of hours automatic.
ideas.revenue_model: Per-member-per-month retention fee, or per-successful-report fee, paid by hospitals, FQHCs and plans. Later, state contracts and a SNAP work-requirement product on the same infrastructure.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The payer is neither the patient nor the state. It is whoever loses revenue when a member drops. The failure is documentation friction, not eligibility. The cheapest evidence source is the member's own gig or payroll account plus the clinic visit itself, which can collect exemption proof for free.
ideas.first_30_days: Choose one state with an early or waiver-driven start and a large FQHC association. Meet revenue-cycle and financial-counseling leads at 5 FQHCs and hospitals. Publish a free state-by-state 'Am I exempt? Do my hours count?' checker to generate leads. Run a manual SMS concierge pilot with 200 members using a spreadsheet and volunteers, and measure on-time reporting rate. Convert the best result into a signed letter of intent for a per-retained-member fee.

ideas.title: Loss-Draft Concierge for Disaster Rebuilds
ideas.one_liner: A draw desk that gets the insurance money for a destroyed house out of the mortgage servicer's restricted account and into the rebuild, paid by the contractors who need cash to start.
ideas.customer: Mortgaged homeowners whose houses were destroyed or damaged by fire, flood or storm pay $1,500-3,000 flat or about 1% of proceeds. Rebuild contractors pay 1.5-2.5% of each accelerated draw.
ideas.problem: When a mortgaged house is destroyed, insurance checks are made out to both the owner and the servicer. The servicer parks the money in a loss-draft account and releases it in inspection-gated stages, each requiring a contract, contractor license proof, permits, lien waivers, W-9s and photos. Homeowners cannot assemble the packet. Contractors will not start without money. Families pay rent and a mortgage on a lot with nothing on it. Rebuild fraud thrives in the gap.
ideas.solution: A draw desk that takes the servicer's letter and builds the draw packet in the exact format the servicer wants. It verifies the contractor's license, collects conditional and unconditional lien waivers on the state statutory forms, books inspections, submits, and chases weekly. It escalates to servicer executive complaint lines and state regulators. It ties every disbursement to milestone photos and waivers so the homeowner is protected from paying for work not done. It never holds the funds, which avoids money-transmitter issues. Later add bridge financing against expected draws.
ideas.why_now: The January 2025 Los Angeles fires destroyed roughly 16,000 structures and rebuilds are now at peak permit and construction paperwork. Storm and flood rebuilds continue in Texas, North Carolina and Florida, and every season adds more. Additional-living-expense coverage has clocks that expire, which makes delay costly. AI document handling makes lien-waiver, permit and inspection-photo checks cheap for a small team.
ideas.revenue_model: Flat rebuild-admin package or about 1% of proceeds from homeowners. A per-draw acceleration fee of 1.5-2.5% from contractors. Later, a spread on bridge loans and referral revenue from lenders and builders.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck is not the insurer. The money already exists and is locked behind paperwork the homeowner cannot produce. Public adjusters take about 10% to fight the insurer but nobody specializes in this second fight. The hidden buyer is the contractor, whose cash flow decides whether the site ever starts.
ideas.first_30_days: Join fire-survivor community groups and rebuild nonprofits in one affected area. Offer a free draw-packet review to the first 10 households. Sign 3 rebuild contractors whose draws are stalled. Charge a flat fee only after the first draw is released. Document days-to-funds before and after as your proof, then take the case studies to the next disaster market.

ideas.title: Live Doom-Pile Sessions for Avoided Paperwork
ideas.one_liner: A scheduled video session where a calm, admin-savvy host sits with you while you open the unopened mail pile, triages it, and gets the scary items handled before you hang up.
ideas.customer: Adults 25-55 with ADHD, anxiety, depression, recent bereavement or new-parent overload pay $59 per session or $89 a month for two sessions. Employer benefit programs, credit unions and probate attorneys pay for seats.
ideas.problem: Millions of people leave envelopes and portal notifications unopened because not knowing is more comfortable than knowing. Late fees, collections, missed renewals and tax notices escalate. The avoidance is emotional, so productivity apps and reminder tools do not touch it.
ideas.solution: A 45-minute weekly 'Admin Sunday' session. Members upload photos of the pile beforehand and AI produces a triage card (ignore, do this month, act by Friday). A trained host, such as a former paralegal, bookkeeper or benefits caseworker, sits with the member on camera as each envelope is opened. Three actions get done in the session, such as calling with a script, setting up a payment plan, or filing a form. The member leaves with a 'Nothing Scary' summary. A mail-forwarding tier serves people who cannot face even the session.
ideas.why_now: Adult ADHD diagnoses have surged and body-doubling is mainstream on TikTok and in tools like Focusmate. LLMs make triage and drafting nearly free, so one human can run 6-8 sessions a day and the business keeps a healthy margin. Collections on federal student loans restarted in 2025, raising the stakes of ignored mail. Consumers now value human presence precisely because AI can read the letter but cannot sit next to you.
ideas.revenue_model: $89 monthly subscription for two sessions, $59 a la carte. Hosts are paid $28-35 an hour, giving roughly 55-60% gross margin. B2B seats at $12-20 per employee per month for EAP and financial-wellness buyers.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The product is courage with a witness, not productivity. People will pay to discover bad news in the company of someone calm. Silent co-working apps do not solve this because the body double is not allowed to help, and AI alone cannot absorb the emotion of opening the envelope.
ideas.first_30_days: Post in ADHD and adulting communities and make short 'doom pile' videos. Run 10 free consented live sessions to create content and testimonials. Sell $49 founding-member sessions through Stripe and run on Zoom and Google Drive. Recruit 5 hosts from retired paralegal and bookkeeper groups. Goal: 15 paying subscribers by day 30 and 30 by day 60.

ideas.title: The Neutral Verdict on Dad's Driving
ideas.one_liner: An independent on-road evaluation of an aging parent's driving that gives adult children a credentialed Green, Yellow or Red verdict, plus a graduated plan so nobody has to be the villain about the keys.
ideas.customer: Adult children aged 45-65 of drivers 75+ pay $349-449 per evaluation and $12 a month for monitoring. Later buyers are auto insurers, Medicare Advantage plans and long-term-care insurers.
ideas.problem: Taking away the keys is one of the most dreaded family confrontations. The parent hears loss of independence and the child becomes the villain. Doctors rarely intervene, DMV medical review is slow, and driver-rehab specialists have months-long waitlists. Families wait for a crash. AAA and AARP offer generic tips, not an individual, defensible verdict.
ideas.solution: Frame it as a safety tune-up and send a certified evaluator, an OT with driver-rehab credentials or trained retired instructors under OT supervision. They ride in the parent's own car on a standardized 45-minute route with scoring for gap judgment, lane keeping, hesitation and scanning, plus a brief cognitive screen. The report gives a Green, Yellow or Red verdict. Yellow means no night, highway or rush hour with a recheck in six months, optionally verified by connected-car data or a cheap OBD dongle with the parent's consent. Red comes with a transition kit of robotaxi and rideshare credits, grocery and pharmacy delivery, and a senior-center pass, so retirement feels like an upgrade. The evaluator is advisory only and DMV referral is optional.
ideas.why_now: The oldest baby boomers turn 80 in 2026. Robotaxis now operate commercially in a growing list of US metros, so a real off-ramp finally exists. Connected-car APIs make objective driving data possible with consent. Scarce driver-rehab specialists can be leveraged with standardized scoring and remote review.
ideas.revenue_model: $349-449 per evaluation, a $12 monthly monitoring subscription for Yellow-zone drivers, and referral or ride-credit margin on the transition kit. B2B per-evaluation contracts with insurers and Medicare Advantage plans that want fewer elder-driver claims.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The product is a third party who absorbs the blame. Families are buying relational insurance, not a road test. The recurring money is in the Yellow zone, where a graduated restriction plan needs ongoing verification, which turns a one-off confrontation into a subscription.
ideas.first_30_days: Partner with 2-3 driver-rehab OTs in one metro, plus elder-law attorneys and geriatric care managers for referrals. Build the scoring sheet from published road-test protocols. Get liability coverage and a consent script. Run 10 evaluations at a $249 intro price. Recruit through caregiver-support groups and Facebook groups for adult children of aging parents. Publish anonymized case studies.
